answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens and form an interaction graph audited via topological cut verifications. A sparrow agent validates peer throughput, while random multi-agent committees audit network cuts. Any detected Sybil cluster faces instant stake slashing, turning forged identities into a worthless relic. Because establishing dense cross-cluster cuts requires exponential stake scaling up to an unachievable zenith, attacker costs become strictly superlinear.
